title: RngRange signed-overflow UB for spans > 2^31 violates the ODN-10 well-defined-math contract the header itself claims
detail: For spans > 2^31 the draw can exceed INT32_MAX; the int32_t cast wraps negative and Lo + negative overflows — UB the spine explicitly forbids. spine_check.cpp:110 exercises this exact span; it passes only via benign wrap.
recommended_fix: Do the add-back in int64 and cast once: return static_cast<int32_t>(static_cast<int64_t>(Lo) + ((static_cast<uint64_t>(RngNext(R)) * Span) >> 32)); — result is always value-preserving, UB-free.

title: StateHash's fixed 64-byte stack buffer silently degrades to a constant hash once slice-1 grows serialization past 64 bytes
detail: Slice-1 adds topology/packet pools to the state; once Needed > 64, SerializeState returns 0 and every state hashes to FNV64_OFFSET. Replay-equality still 'passes'; only divergence tests catch it, indirectly and confusingly.
recommended_fix: Tie buffer size to the format: one shared constexpr (e.g. PP_SERIALIZED_STATE_MAX) used by SerializeState's Needed and StateHash's buffer, or make StateHash fail loudly when SerializeState returns 0.

title: PacketPlumberEditor declares an unused UnrealEd dependency
evidence:
PacketPlumberEditor.Build.cs:10-17:
		PublicDependencyModuleNames.AddRange(new string[]
		{
			"Core",
			"CoreUObject",
			"Engine",
			"UnrealEd",
			"PacketPlumberCore",
		});
All includes in the module:
Source/PacketPlumberEditor/PPProbeCommandlet.h:15:#include "Commandlets/Commandlet.h"
Source/PacketPlumberEditor/PPProbeCommandlet.cpp:11:#include "Misc/FileHelper.h"
Source/PacketPlumberEditor/PPProbeCommandlet.cpp:12:#include "Misc/Paths.h"
detail: Nothing in the module includes UnrealEd headers (UCommandlet is Engine; FileHelper/Paths are Core). The heavyweight editor dependency adds build cost and coupling the headless commandlet module does not need.
recommended_fix: Drop UnrealEd from PublicDependencyModuleNames; re-add only when a real UnrealEd include lands (future editor toolset wrappers).

title: CoreTests module comment mislabels the module type as 'Developer' while the uproject declares UncookedOnly
detail: Declared type is UncookedOnly, not Developer — and Developer-type modules DO load in packaged Development builds. The mislabel misleads future module-type decisions about where the tests can load.
recommended_fix: Fix the comment to state UncookedOnly (loads in editor and uncooked targets, never cooked/shipped).

title: Golden-probe JSON schema is defined independently in three places
evidence:
tests/spine_check.cpp:252:
		std::printf("{\"seed\":42,\"ticks\":100,\"tick_nonce\":%u,\"state_hash\":\"%016llx\",\"rng_first4\":[%u,%u,%u,%u],\"save_magic\":\"PPUE\",\"save_version\":1}\n",
PPProbeCommandlet.cpp:89-91:
		const FString Json = FString::Printf(
			TEXT("{\"seed\":%llu,\"ticks\":%d,\"tick_nonce\":%u,\"state_hash\":\"%016llx\",\"rng_first4\":[%u,%u,%u,%u]"
					 ",\"save_magic\":\"PPUE\",\"save_version\":1}\n"),
scripts/compare-golden.sh:32:
KEYS = ("seed", "ticks", "tick_nonce", "state_hash", "save_magic", "save_version", "rng_first4")
detail: The cross-runner contract schema lives in spine_check.cpp, PPProbeCommandlet.cpp, and compare-golden.sh KEYS. Adding a field requires three synchronized edits; drift surfaces only as a gate-7 mismatch (engine-gated).
recommended_fix: Emit the probe JSON from one shared spine-header helper (both runners compile the same headers by design), or document the KEYS tuple as the canonical schema.
